title: How do Organisms Reproduce?
seo_title: How do Organisms Reproduce? Class 10 Science Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Chapter 7)
standard_code: Class 10, Chapter 7: How do Organisms Reproduce?
standard_text: Reproduction in animals and plants (asexual and sexual), reproductive health – need and methods of family planning, safe sex vs HIV/AIDS, child bearing and women's health.
meta_desc: Free CBSE Class 10 Science worksheets for NCERT Chapter 7: fission, budding, regeneration, spores, vegetative propagation, parts of a flower, human reproduction and reproductive health. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Asexual: one parent, copies. Sexual: two parents, variation.
key_sub: Ovule → seed, ovary → fruit after fertilisation.
body_html:
How to think about it

In asexual reproduction one parent gives offspring almost identical to itself: fission (Amoeba, Leishmania, Plasmodium), budding (Hydra, yeast), regeneration (Planaria), fragmentation (Spirogyra), spores (Rhizopus) and vegetative propagation (potato, Bryophyllum).

In sexual reproduction, gametes with half the chromosomes fuse to form a zygote, giving variation. In flowers, pollen from the anther reaches the stigma, a pollen tube carries the male gamete to the ovule, and after fertilisation the ovule becomes the seed and the ovary the fruit.

Example

How does Plasmodium reproduce?

it divides into many cells at once

Answer: multiple fission

Example

After fertilisation, what does the ovary become?

the ovules become seeds inside it

Answer: the fruit

Common mistakes

  • Mixing up pollination and fertilisation.
  • Thinking yeast reproduces by fission.
  • Saying the ovary becomes the seed.

faq.q: Where does fertilisation take place in humans?
faq.a: In the oviduct (fallopian tube); the embryo then implants in the uterus.

items.q: How does Spirogyra reproduce?
c: vegetative propagation from buds (eyes) on the tuber
vegetative propagation from buds on the leaf margin
items.e: Spirogyra: fragmentation.

items.q: How does Planaria reproduce?
c: only vegetative propagation, because it makes no seeds
vegetative propagation from buds on the leaf margin
items.e: Planaria: regeneration.

items.q: Which organism reproduces by budding?

items.q: Which part of a flower or seed does this: holding up the anther?
items.e: The filament: holding up the anther.

items.q: Which part of a flower or seed does this: storing food for the embryo?
items.e: The cotyledons: storing food for the embryo.

items.q: Which part of a flower or seed does this: containing the egg cell; it becomes the seed?
items.e: The ovule: containing the egg cell; it becomes the seed.

items.q: Which part of a flower or seed does this: protecting the flower in the bud stage?
items.e: The sepals: protecting the flower in the bud stage.

items.q: What is the job of the stamen in a flower or seed?
c: protecting the flower in the bud stage
the part of the embryo that becomes the shoot
the male part, which makes pollen
containing ovules; it becomes the fruit
items.e: The stamen: the male part, which makes pollen.

items.q: Which part of a flower or seed does this: containing ovules; it becomes the fruit?
items.e: The ovary: containing ovules; it becomes the fruit.

items.q: Which part of a flower or seed does this: the male part, which makes pollen?
items.e: The stamen: the male part, which makes pollen.

items.q: Which part of a flower or seed does this: receiving pollen grains?
items.e: The stigma: receiving pollen grains.

items.q: What is the job of the cotyledons in a flower or seed?
c: protecting the embryo inside the seed
attracting insects with a sugary liquid
items.e: The cotyledons: storing food for the embryo.

items.q: Which part of a flower or seed does this: protecting the embryo inside the seed?
items.e: The seed coat: protecting the embryo inside the seed.

items.q: What is the job of the plumule in a flower or seed?
c: the part of the embryo that becomes the shoot
protecting the flower in the bud stage
items.e: The plumule: the part of the embryo that becomes the shoot.

items.q: What is the job of the petals in a flower or seed?
c: the part of the embryo that becomes the shoot
attracting insects with a sugary liquid
containing the egg cell; it becomes the seed
items.e: The petals: attracting insects for pollination.

items.q: What is the job of the seed coat in a flower or seed?
c: protecting the flower in the bud stage
containing ovules; it becomes the fruit
protecting the embryo inside the seed
the part of the embryo that becomes the root
items.e: The seed coat: protecting the embryo inside the seed.

items.q: What is the job of the ovule in a flower or seed?
c: protecting the embryo inside the seed
containing the egg cell; it becomes the seed
the male part, which makes pollen
items.e: The ovule: containing the egg cell; it becomes the seed.

items.q: Which part of a flower or seed does this: attracting insects with a sugary liquid?
items.e: Nectar: attracting insects with a sugary liquid.

items.q: What is the job of nectar in a flower or seed?
c: attracting insects with a sugary liquid
protecting the flower in the bud stage
items.e: Nectar: attracting insects with a sugary liquid.

containing the egg cell; it becomes the seed

items.q: Which part of a flower or seed does this: attracting insects for pollination?
items.e: The petals: attracting insects for pollination.

items.q: What is the job of the filament in a flower or seed?
c: the male part, which makes pollen
containing the egg cell; it becomes the seed
protecting the embryo inside the seed
items.e: The filament: holding up the anther.

items.q: Why does the number of chromosomes stay the same from parents to offspring?
c: gametes have half the number of chromosomes
items.e: Fusion restores the full number.

items.q: What is the job of the uterus?
c: where the embryo implants and grows
connecting the embryo to the placenta
carrying both urine and sperm out of the body
items.e: The uterus: where the embryo implants and grows.

items.q: Why does a fertilised egg divide many times?
c: to form the embryo with many cells
items.e: Cells then specialise to form organs.

items.q: Which part of the human reproductive system does this: carrying both urine and sperm out of the body?
c: the seminal vesicles and prostate gland
items.e: The urethra in males: carrying both urine and sperm out of the body.

items.q: Why is prenatal sex determination banned in India?
c: it is misused for female foeticide, harming the sex ratio
items.e: A healthy society needs a balanced sex ratio.

items.q: Which part of the human reproductive system does this: passing food and oxygen from mother to embryo and removing wastes?
items.e: The placenta: passing food and oxygen from mother to embryo and removing wastes.

items.q: What is the job of the ovaries?
c: carrying both urine and sperm out of the body
making eggs and the hormone oestrogen
adding fluid that nourishes sperm and helps them move
where the embryo implants and grows
items.e: The ovaries: making eggs and the hormone oestrogen.

items.q: What is germination?
c: the growth of a seed into a seedling
items.e: It needs water, air and warmth.

items.q: Which part of the human reproductive system does this: keeping the testes at a lower temperature than the body?
items.e: The scrotum: keeping the testes at a lower temperature than the body.

items.q: What is a zygote?
c: the cell formed when a male and female gamete fuse
items.e: It divides to form the embryo.

items.q: Why does reproduction need energy?
c: making new cells and gametes uses energy
items.e: Organisms grow and repair too.

items.q: Why do the walls of the uterus thicken every month?
c: to store food for the mother
to prepare to receive a fertilised egg
items.e: If there is no fertilisation, the lining breaks down (menstruation).

items.q: What is the advantage of vegetative propagation?
c: plants grow faster and are exactly like the parent
items.e: It is used for plants that do not make viable seeds.

items.q: Which part of the human reproductive system does this: connecting the embryo to the placenta?
items.e: The umbilical cord: connecting the embryo to the placenta.

items.q: What is the job of the placenta?
c: passing food and oxygen from mother to embryo and removing wastes
carrying sperm from the testes towards the urethra
receiving sperm and forming the birth canal
items.e: The placenta: passing food and oxygen from mother to embryo and removing wastes.

items.q: What is the job of the vagina?
c: adding fluid that nourishes sperm and helps them move
receiving sperm and forming the birth canal
the female gamete that fuses with a sperm
items.e: The vagina: receiving sperm and forming the birth canal.

items.q: What is the job of the egg (ovum)?
c: carrying sperm from the testes towards the urethra
receiving sperm and forming the birth canal
passing food and oxygen from mother to embryo and removing wastes
the female gamete that fuses with a sperm
items.e: The egg (ovum): the female gamete that fuses with a sperm.

items.q: What is the job of the urethra in males?
c: receiving sperm and forming the birth canal
keeping the testes at a lower temperature than the body
where the embryo implants and grows
carrying both urine and sperm out of the body
items.e: The urethra in males: carrying both urine and sperm out of the body.

items.q: Which part of the human reproductive system does this: making sperm and testosterone?
c: the seminal vesicles and prostate gland
items.e: The testes: making sperm and testosterone.

items.q: What is the job of the vas deferens?
c: carrying sperm from the testes towards the urethra
adding fluid that nourishes sperm and helps them move
where the embryo implants and grows
items.e: The vas deferens: carrying sperm from the testes towards the urethra.

items.q: What causes HIV-AIDS?
items.e: Gonorrhoea and syphilis are bacterial; warts and HIV-AIDS are viral.

items.q: What causes syphilis?
items.e: Gonorrhoea and syphilis are bacterial; warts and HIV-AIDS are viral.

items.q: What is copper-T?
c: surgery that blocks the fallopian tubes in females
a hormonal method that changes the hormone balance so eggs are not released
a device placed in the uterus to prevent pregnancy
surgery that blocks the vas deferens in males
items.e: Copper-T: a device placed in the uterus to prevent pregnancy.

items.q: Why can't all organisms reproduce by regeneration?
c: only simple organisms have specialised cells that can make every type of tissue
items.e: Complex animals cannot regrow a whole body.

items.q: What is the number of chromosomes in a human gamete?
items.e: Body cells have 46 (23 pairs).

items.q: What is tubectomy?
c: a device placed in the uterus to prevent pregnancy
a hormonal method that changes the hormone balance so eggs are not released
surgery that blocks the fallopian tubes in females
a barrier method that also helps prevent sexually transmitted infections
items.e: Tubectomy: surgery that blocks the fallopian tubes in females.

items.q: Why is DNA copying important in reproduction?
c: it passes the body design to the offspring, with small variations
items.e: Variation helps a species survive changes.

items.q: What is oral pills?
c: surgery that blocks the fallopian tubes in females
surgery that blocks the vas deferens in males
a hormonal method that changes the hormone balance so eggs are not released
a device placed in the uterus to prevent pregnancy
items.e: Oral pills: a hormonal method that changes the hormone balance so eggs are not released.

items.q: What is menstruation?
c: the shedding of the thickened lining of the uterus when there is no fertilisation
items.e: It happens about every 28 days.

items.q: What is tissue culture?
c: growing new plants from a few cells of a plant in a nutrient medium
items.e: It is used for ornamental plants such as orchids.

items.q: Why is variation useful for a species?
c: some individuals may survive if the environment changes
items.e: It is the basis of evolution.

items.q: What is pollination?
c: the joining of the sperm and egg
the transfer of pollen from an anther to a stigma
items.e: Wind, water and insects carry pollen.

items.q: What happens after fertilisation in a flower?
c: the ovule becomes a seed and the ovary becomes a fruit
items.e: The zygote grows into the embryo.

items.q: What is condoms?
c: a barrier method that also helps prevent sexually transmitted infections
surgery that blocks the fallopian tubes in females
a hormonal method that changes the hormone balance so eggs are not released
a device placed in the uterus to prevent pregnancy
items.e: Condoms: a barrier method that also helps prevent sexually transmitted infections.

items.q: What are spores?
c: small structures with a thick wall that can survive harsh conditions and grow into new organisms
items.e: Rhizopus makes spores in sporangia.

items.q: How long does a human baby develop in the uterus?
items.e: Birth happens by rhythmic contraction of the uterus muscles.

items.q: What causes warts?
items.e: Gonorrhoea and syphilis are bacterial; warts and HIV-AIDS are viral.

items.q: What is the advantage of sexual reproduction over asexual reproduction?
c: it gives more variation in the offspring
items.e: Variation helps a species adapt.

items.q: What is vasectomy?
c: surgery that blocks the vas deferens in males
a barrier method that also helps prevent sexually transmitted infections
surgery that blocks the fallopian tubes in females
a hormonal method that changes the hormone balance so eggs are not released
items.e: Vasectomy: surgery that blocks the vas deferens in males.

items.q: What causes gonorrhoea?
items.e: Gonorrhoea and syphilis are bacterial; warts and HIV-AIDS are viral.

items.q: Which organism reproduces by binary fission (in any plane)?
items.e: Amoeba: binary fission (in any plane).

items.q: Which plant is grown from layering a branch into the soil?
items.e: Jasmine: layering a branch into the soil.

items.q: Which plant is grown from grafting a shoot onto a rooted plant?
items.e: Mango (grafted): grafting a shoot onto a rooted plant.

items.q: Which part of a flower or seed does this: connecting the stigma to the ovary, through which the pollen tube grows?
items.e: The style: connecting the stigma to the ovary, through which the pollen tube grows.

items.q: Which part is used to grow new money plant plants?
c: layering a branch into the soil
items.e: Money plant: a stem cutting.

items.q: What is the difference between self-pollination and cross-pollination?
c: self: pollen goes to a stigma of the same flower or plant; cross: to another plant
self needs insects, cross does not
items.e: Cross-pollination gives more variation.

items.q: Which plant is grown from a stem cutting?
items.e: Sugarcane: a stem cutting.

items.q: Which part of a flower or seed does this: the part of the embryo that becomes the shoot?
items.e: The plumule: the part of the embryo that becomes the shoot.

items.q: Which part is used to grow new mango (grafted) plants?
c: grafting a shoot onto a rooted plant
layering a branch into the soil
items.e: Mango (grafted): grafting a shoot onto a rooted plant.

items.q: What is a unisexual flower?
c: a flower with either stamens or a pistil, such as papaya or watermelon
a flower with both stamens and pistil
items.e: Hibiscus and mustard are bisexual.

items.q: How does Planaria regenerate?
c: each cut piece grows into a complete organism using specialised cells
it buds from the head only
items.e: Not all organisms can do this.

items.q: Which part is used to grow new jasmine plants?
c: layering a branch into the soil
items.e: Jasmine: layering a branch into the soil.

items.q: Which part is used to grow new Bryophyllum plants?
c: grafting a shoot onto a rooted plant
items.e: Bryophyllum: buds on the leaf margins.

items.q: What is the function of the pollen tube?
c: carrying the male gamete to the ovule
items.e: It grows down through the style.

items.q: Which plant is grown from a root?
items.e: Sweet potato: a root.

items.q: What is the job of the ovary in a flower or seed?
c: connecting the stigma to the ovary, through which the pollen tube grows
containing ovules; it becomes the fruit
items.e: The ovary: containing ovules; it becomes the fruit.

items.q: Which plant is grown from a stem tuber with buds (eyes)?
items.e: Potato: a stem tuber with buds (eyes).

items.q: Which part of a flower or seed does this: making pollen grains?
items.e: The anther: making pollen grains.

items.q: Which plant is grown from a bulb?
items.e: Onion: a bulb.

items.q: How does Leishmania reproduce?
items.e: Leishmania: binary fission (in a definite plane).
